1. Ants are among the most successful animals on Earth.
2. There are over 12,000 known species of ants.
3. Ants can lift objects 50 times their own body weight.
4. Ants have been around for over 100 million years.
5. Ant colonies can contain millions of individual insects.
6. Ants communicate using chemical signals called pheromones.
7. Ants have two stomachs, one for themselves and one to share.
8. A single ant colony can spread across several miles.
9. Ants are found on every continent except Antarctica.
10. Ant queens can live up to 30 years in some species.
11. Male ants only live for a few weeks.
12. Ants do not have ears but can feel vibrations.
13. Some ants farm fungi as a food source.
14. Ants are capable of recognizing themselves in mirrors.
15. An ant's brain contains about 250,000 neurons.
16. Ants sleep very little, only brief naps during the day.
17. Some ants can navigate using the sun's position.
18. Leafcutter ants cut leaves to feed to their fungal gardens.
19. Ants have been observed engaging in organized warfare.
20. Carpenter ants can damage wooden structures in homes.
21. Fire ants can form living rafts to survive floods.
22. Ants taste with their feet to identify food sources.
23. Some ant species are parasitic to other ant colonies.
24. Ants create highways to transport food efficiently.
25. The combined biomass of all ants equals that of all humans.
26. Ants can survive in extreme temperatures and environments.
27. Some ants practice slavery by raiding other colonies.
28. Ant colonies have distinct social hierarchies and roles.
29. Ants use trail markers to lead other ants to food.
30. Some ants can explode to defend their colony.
31. Ants have been used in medical research for centuries.
32. Bullet ants have one of the most painful insect stings.
33. Ants can create their own antibiotics to fight infections.
34. Some ants build elaborate underground tunnel systems.
35. Ants have been shown to have a sense of time.
36. Weaver ants use silk from their larvae to build nests.
37. Ants can adapt to new environments very quickly.
38. Some ant species have eyes while others are blind.
39. Ants have been observed caring for sick colony members.
40. Ants will continue to thrive long after humans vanish.

# The Lost Forager

In a sprawling underground city beneath the old oak tree, an ant named Cipher worked as a forager. She was faster than most, with a keen sense for finding food sources that others missed. One morning, while exploring beyond the familiar pheromone trails, Cipher discovered something extraordinary: a cache of seeds three times larger than any her colony had ever found.
